chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hisham ibn Salim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
It suffices as a sin for a person that he wastes/neglects those whom he provides for.

key_terms.يضيع: To waste, neglect, squander, let go to ruin — used for abandoning one's duty of care
key_terms.يعوله: Those whom he provides for, dependants under his guardianship (wife, children, elderly parents)

ai.seo_question: What does Imam al-Sadiq say about neglecting one's dependants in al-Kafi?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) delivers a sharp warning: merely neglecting one's dependants — those under one's financial care and guardianship — is itself sufficient to constitute a grave sin. The teaching reflects the Shia emphasis on family obligations as religious duties; failing to properly care for one's household is not a minor fault but a sin in its own right. The phrase 'it suffices as a sin' echoes a well-known prophetic formulation used to signal that the named act alone is enough to condemn a person.
